title.zh: 卷一百〇八 列傳第三十八: 方技
title.raw: 卷一百〇八 列傳第三十八: 方技 Volume 108 Biographies 38: Divination

sentences.zh: 方技 ○直魯古王白魏璘耶律敵魯耶律乙不哥

translations.literal: Arts and Techniques ○ Zhilugu, Wang Bai, Wei Lin, Yelü Diru, Yelü Yibuge
translations.idiomatic: Arts and Techniques ○ Zhilugu, Wang Bai, Wei Lin, Yelü Diru, and Yelü Yibuge

sentences.zh: 孔子稱「小道必有可觀」，醫卜是已。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Even the lesser paths must have something worth viewing" — medicine and divination are precisely such.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that even minor arts must have something worth seeing — medicine and divination are cases in point.

sentences.zh: 醫以濟夭劄，卜以決猶豫，皆有補於國，有惠於民。

translations.literal: Medicine is used to relieve premature death and disaster; divination is used to resolve hesitation; both have benefit for the state and grace for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine eases untimely death and suffering; divination settles doubt and indecision — both serve the state and bring benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 前史錄而不遺，故傳。

translations.literal: Previous histories recorded them without omission; therefore they are transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories recorded such men without leaving them out; that is why they appear here.

sentences.zh: 直魯古，吐谷渾人。

translations.literal: Zhilugu was a man of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilugu was a native of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖破吐谷渾，一騎士棄橐反射，不中而去。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Taizu defeated Tuyuhun, one rider abandoned a bag and shot back at it; he missed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Taizu routed the Tuyuhun, one rider cast down a bag and shot back at it; his arrow missed, and he rode away.

sentences.zh: 及追兵開橐視之，中得一嬰兒，即直魯古也。

translations.literal: When the pursuing troops opened the bag and looked, they obtained an infant within — this was Zhilugu.
translations.idiomatic: When the pursuers opened the bag and looked inside, they found an infant — Zhilugu himself.

sentences.zh: 因所俘者問其故，乃知射橐者嬰之父也。

translations.literal: Through those who had been captured they asked the reason, and thus knew that the one who shot the bag was the infant's father.
translations.idiomatic: They questioned the captives about what had happened and learned that the man who shot the bag was the child's father.

sentences.zh: 世善醫，雖馬上視疾，亦知標本。

translations.literal: For generations they excelled at medicine; even when examining illness on horseback, he knew root and branch.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long practiced medicine; even when treating the sick from horseback, he could distinguish root cause from symptom.

sentences.zh: 意不欲子為人所得，欲殺之耳。

translations.literal: His intention was that he did not wish his son to be taken by others — he had meant to kill him, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: He had not wanted his son to fall into enemy hands and had meant only to kill the child.

sentences.zh: 由是進於太祖，淳欽皇后收養之。

translations.literal: Because of this he was presented to Taizu, and Empress Chunqin adopted and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then brought before Taizu, and Empress Chunqin took him in and raised him.

sentences.zh: 長亦能醫，專事針灸。

translations.literal: When he grew up he too could practice medicine, specializing in acupuncture and moxibustion.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he too practiced medicine, devoting himself to acupuncture and moxibustion.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，以太醫給侍。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time he served as imperial physician in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he served as an imperial physician in attendance.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰《脈訣》、《針灸書》，行於世。

translations.literal: He once compiled Pulse Diagnosis and A Book on Acupuncture and Moxibustion, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote Pulse Diagnosis and A Book on Acupuncture and Moxibustion, both of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 年九十卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety.

sentences.zh: 魏璘，不知何郡人，以卜名世，太宗得於汴。

translations.literal: Wei Lin — it is not known from which commandery he came; he made a name for himself through divination, and Taizong obtained him at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lin was a man of unknown native commandery who won fame through divination; Taizong acquired him at Bian.

sentences.zh: 天祿元年，上命馳馬較遲疾，以為勝負。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianlu, the emperor ordered horses raced to compare speed, taking that as victory or defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianlu, the emperor ordered a horse race to settle the contest by speed.

sentences.zh: 問王白及璘孰勝，白奏曰：「赤者勝。」

translations.literal: He asked Wang Bai and Wei Lin which would win. Bai reported, "The red one will win."
translations.idiomatic: He asked Wang Bai and Wei Lin which horse would win. Bai replied, "The chestnut will win."

sentences.zh: 璘曰：「臣所見，驄馬當勝。」

translations.literal: Lin said, "In my view the piebald horse ought to win."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "As I see it, the gray horse should prevail."

sentences.zh: 既馳，竟如璘言。

translations.literal: After they had raced, it turned out exactly as Lin had said.
translations.idiomatic: When the race was run, the outcome matched Lin's prediction exactly.

sentences.zh: 上異而問之，白曰：「今日火王，故知赤者勝。」

translations.literal: The emperor was astonished and questioned them. Bai said, "Today fire dominates, therefore I knew the red would win."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and questioned them. Bai said, "Fire rules the day, so I knew the chestnut would win."

sentences.zh: 璘曰：「不然，火雖王，而上有煙。

translations.literal: Lin said, "Not so — though fire dominates, there is smoke above it.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "Not so. Fire may rule, but there is smoke above it.

sentences.zh: 以煙察之，青者必勝。」

translations.literal: Observing by the smoke, the green must win."
translations.idiomatic: Judge by the smoke, and the gray horse is sure to prevail."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 五年，察割謀逆，私卜於璘。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Chage plotted rebellion and privately sought divination from Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Chage plotted treason and privately had Lin divine for him.

sentences.zh: 璘始卜，謂曰：「大王之數，得一日矣，宜慎之！」

translations.literal: When Lin first divined, he told him, "Your Lordship's fate has but one day left — you ought to be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: At the first casting Lin told him, "Your Highness's allotted span has but a single day left — take care!"

sentences.zh: 及亂，果敗。

translations.literal: When the disturbance broke out, he was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt came, he was indeed ruined.

sentences.zh: 應歷中，周兵犯燕，上以勝敗問璘。

translations.literal: During Yingli, Zhou troops invaded Yan; the emperor asked Lin about victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yingli era, Zhou forces invaded Yan, and the emperor asked Lin which side would prevail.

sentences.zh: 璘曰：「周姓柴也，燕分火也。

translations.literal: Lin said, "Zhou's surname is Chai, and Yan's allotment is fire.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "Zhou's ruling house bears the surname Chai, and Yan's element is fire.

sentences.zh: 柴入火，必焚。」

translations.literal: Firewood entering fire — it must burn."
translations.idiomatic: Firewood cast into flame must be consumed."

sentences.zh: 其言果驗。

translations.literal: His words were indeed verified.
translations.idiomatic: Events bore out his words.

sentences.zh: 璘嘗為太平王罨撒葛卜僭立事，上聞之，免死，流烏古部。

translations.literal: Lin had once divined on the matter of usurpation for Prince of Taiping Anashige; when the emperor heard of it, he spared his life and exiled him to the Wugu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had once divined for Prince of Taiping Anashige on his bid to seize the throne; when the emperor learned of it, he spared Lin's life but exiled him to the Wugu tribe.

sentences.zh: 一日，節度使召璘，適有獻雙鯉者，戲曰：「君卜此魚何時得食？」

translations.literal: One day the military commissioner summoned Lin; just then someone presented a pair of carp, and in jest he said, "Sir, divine when this fish may be eaten?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the military commissioner summoned Lin; someone had just presented a pair of carp, and in jest he asked, "Can you divine when we shall eat these fish?"

sentences.zh: 璘良久答曰：「公與仆不出今日，有不測禍，奚暇食魚？」

translations.literal: After a long while Lin answered, "Your Lordship and I will not leave today alive — with unforeseen calamity upon us, how would we have leisure to eat fish?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause Lin answered, "My lord and I will not live out the day. With disaster upon us, who has time to eat fish?"

sentences.zh: 亟命烹之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered them cooked.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the fish prepared.

sentences.zh: 未及食，寇至，俱遇害。

translations.literal: Before they could eat, raiders arrived and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could eat, the enemy arrived, and both were slain.

sentences.zh: 耶律敵魯，字撒不碗。

translations.literal: Yelü Diru, courtesy name Sabowan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Diru, courtesy name Sabowan.

sentences.zh: 其先本五院之族，始置宮分，隸焉。

translations.literal: His forebears were originally of the Five Tribes; when the palace estates were first established, they were enrolled therein.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors belonged to the Five Tribes; when the palace estates were first established, they were enrolled there.

sentences.zh: 敵魯精於醫，察形色即知病原。

translations.literal: Diru was skilled in medicine; observing form and complexion he knew the source of the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Diru was a master physician who could tell the source of an illness from a patient's appearance alone.

sentences.zh: 雖不診候，有十全功。

translations.literal: Even without examining or inquiring, he had the efficacy of ten complete cures.
translations.idiomatic: Even without taking the pulse or questioning the patient, his cures were invariably complete.

sentences.zh: 統和初，為大丞相韓德讓所薦，官至節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe he was recommended by Grand Chancellor Han Derang and rose to military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tonghe era he was recommended by Grand Chancellor Han Derang and eventually rose to military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，樞密使耶律斜軫妻有沈痾，易數醫不能治。

translations.literal: Earlier, the wife of Commissioner-in-Chief Yelü Xiezhen had a deep chronic illness; physicians in succession could not cure her.
translations.idiomatic: Once the wife of Commissioner-in-Chief Yelü Xiezhen suffered a grave chronic illness that one physician after another failed to cure.

sentences.zh: 敵魯視之曰：「心有蓄熱，非藥石所及，當以意療。

translations.literal: Diru looked at her and said, "There is accumulated heat in the heart — medicine and stone cannot reach it; she must be treated through the mind.
translations.idiomatic: Diru examined her and said, "Heat is pent up in the heart. Drugs and needles cannot reach it; she must be treated through the mind.

sentences.zh: 因其聵，聒之使狂，用泄其毒則可。」

translations.literal: Because she is deaf, clamor her into madness to vent the poison — then it may be done."
translations.idiomatic: Because she is deaf, deafen her with noise until she goes mad and the poison can be released — then she may recover."

sentences.zh: 於是令大擊鉦鼓於前。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered gongs and drums struck loudly before her.
translations.idiomatic: He then had gongs and drums beaten loudly before her.

sentences.zh: 翌日果狂，叫呼怒罵，力極而止，遂愈。

translations.literal: The next day she indeed went mad, crying out and cursing in rage until strength was exhausted and she stopped — and then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she did go mad, shouting and cursing until her strength gave out; when she fell silent, she was cured.

sentences.zh: 治法多此類，人莫能測。

translations.literal: His methods of treatment were mostly of this kind; people could not fathom them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his cures followed this pattern, and no one could fathom his methods.

sentences.zh: 年八十卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 耶律乙不哥，字習撚，六院郎君古直之後。

translations.literal: Yelü Yibuge, courtesy name Xinian, a descendant of the Langjun Guzhi of the Six Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yibuge, courtesy name Xinian, was a descendant of Langjun Guzhi of the Six Tribes.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，尤長於卜筮，不樂仕進。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and especially excelled at divination and milfoil; he took no pleasure in pursuing office.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning and excelled above all at divination; he took no pleasure in official advancement.

sentences.zh: 嘗為人擇葬地曰：「後三日，有牛乘人逐牛過者，即啟土。」

translations.literal: He once chose a burial site for someone and said, "In three days, when a man borne by an ox driving an ox passes by, then break ground."
translations.idiomatic: He once selected a burial site for a client and said, "In three days, when you see a man carried by an ox driving another ox past this spot, break ground."

sentences.zh: 至期，果一人負乳犢，引牸牛而過。

translations.literal: When the day came, indeed one man carrying a suckling calf led a cow past.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day, a man carrying a nursing calf led a cow past the site.

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「所謂『牛乘人』者，此也。」

translations.literal: The man said, "What was called 'a man borne by an ox' — this is it."
translations.idiomatic: The client said, "So this is the 'man carried by an ox' you foretold."

sentences.zh: 遂啟土。

translations.literal: Thereupon they broke ground.
translations.idiomatic: They broke ground at once.

sentences.zh: 既葬，吉凶盡如其言。

translations.literal: After the burial, fortune and misfortune all came about as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, every turn of fortune and misfortune unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 又為失鷹者占曰：「鷹在汝家東北三十里濼西榆上。」

translations.literal: Again he divined for one who had lost a hawk and said, "The hawk is thirty li northeast of your home, on an elm west of the marsh."
translations.idiomatic: He also divined for a man who had lost his hawk and said, "Your hawk is on an elm west of the marsh, thirty li northeast of your home."

sentences.zh: 往求之，果得。

translations.literal: Going to seek it, he indeed obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: The man went to look and found the bird exactly where Yibuge had said.

sentences.zh: 當時占候無不驗。

translations.literal: In those days there was no divination of omens that did not prove true.
translations.idiomatic: In his day there was no omen he read that did not come true.

sentences.zh: 論曰：方技，術者也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Arts and techniques are skills.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Arts and techniques are crafts.

sentences.zh: 茍精其業而不畔於道，君子必取焉。

translations.literal: If one masters one's craft and does not depart from the Way, the gentleman will certainly esteem such a one.
translations.idiomatic: If a man masters his craft without straying from the Way, the gentleman will surely value him.

sentences.zh: 直魯古、王白、耶律敵魯無大得失，錄之宜矣。

translations.literal: Zhilugu, Wang Bai, and Yelü Diru had no great gains or losses — to record them is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilugu, Wang Bai, and Yelü Diru committed no great wrongs or merits — it is right that they be recorded.

sentences.zh: 魏璘為察割卜謀逆，為罨撒葛卜僭立，罪在不貰，雖有寸長，亦奚足取哉。

translations.literal: Wei Lin divined for Chage's plot of rebellion and for Anashige's usurpation — crimes unpardonable; though he had some small merit, what was there worth taking?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lin divined for Chage's treason and for Anashige's bid for the throne — offenses beyond pardon. However small his talents, what was there to esteem?

sentences.zh: 存而弗削，為來者戒。

translations.literal: Preserved yet not expunged — a warning for those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: His account is kept rather than struck out, as a warning to those who follow.
